messages:
erin: heads-up — hit a weird edgecase with safetensors loading during a canary rollout. manifest.json was present but one shard object 0/12 returned 404 intermittently, loader fell back to a partial stream path and produced corrupt weights (no checksum mismatch).
sam_k: ouch. can you paste the loader log? is this on our s3 mirror or upstream bucket?
erin: mirror. repro steps are quick: create a manifest that references shard-0000..00011, then atomically delete one shard and reupload while a warmup is in progress. loader log: ```
[2025-11-12T10:05:12Z] loader: resolving manifest -> found 12 shards
[2025-11-12T10:05:12Z] loader: starting parallel fetch (n=4)
[2025-11-12T10:05:13Z] http: GET /s3/mirror/shard-0005 -> 404
[2025-11-12T10:05:13Z] loader: falling back to stream-path for shard-0005
[2025-11-12T10:05:14Z] loader: mapped shard bytes into GPU memory
[2025-11-12T10:05:14Z] runtime: error: malformed kernel input (shape mismatch)
```
no explicit checksum failure — the loader accepted bytes from the stream fallback and downstream compute crashed.
maria-r: is this the index-first vs streaming debate again? if we accept a manifest as authoritative but shards are missing, we need a safety-net.
zane: agree. two orthogonal options: 1) index-first strict: verify existence+checksums for all shards before any mapping; fail fast and require manifest/atomic semantics. 2) progressive-accept with guard: map only shards that verify, and keep the model in "partial" state until all shards verified; route requests to fallback model variant or queued warmup.
erin: option 2 is less disruptive for canaries but we need a safety mechanism to detect corrupt bytes vs transient 404s. currently we conflate missing vs partial writes.
devon: proposal: add a per-shard preflight that does HEAD + etag/size, with a short retry window (200ms x 3) and if the shard still missing, mark shard state = MISSING. then: a) if strict mode -> abort warmup; b) if tolerant mode -> wire in a verification step after mapping that reads a small header region and validates a 64-bit manifest checksum embedded in the shard (we can reserve the first 8 bytes).
sam_k: embedding a 64-bit marker in shard header sounds invasive for safetensors. can we instead compute a fast rolling checksum of first N bytes from object storage without changing formats?
zane: yes, read-first-N is fine. just need to standardize N (like 4k) and store the expected rolling checksum in the manifest fields (manifest already has per-shard size + optional digest). if digest missing, treat as unknown and require strict mode.
 erin: agreed. also: add a transparent retry policy on GET that prefers alternate endpoints (mirror -> origin -> presigned CDN). that avoids transient 404s during background reconciliation.
maria-r: this sounds like a compatibility path: default to strict for Dedicated/Private (enterprise customers want deterministic fails) and default to tolerant for Hosted canaries. we should expose loader config: {mode: strict|tolerant, preflight: true|false, checksum_nbytes: 4096, retry_policy: [mirror,origin,cdn]}
 devon: implementation notes: keep memory mapping orthogonal — map only after preflight success or after verified-read. avoid mapping a zero-length file. atomic swap pattern: upload to shard.tmp then rename to shard so HEAD+GET semantics are reliable. also add a short tombstone TTL for deletes (so manifests referencing deleted shards fail visibly).
sam_k: who picks up the manifest schema upgrade to include optional "preflight_digest"? @maria-r?
maria-r: I can sketch the manifest delta today. backward compatible: new manifest field "preflight_digest": {shard-0005: "sha256:abcd..."} and loader will fallback if digest absent. we'll add schema version bump to 2.1.
erin: tests to add: 1) concurrent upload+warmup repro harness, 2) mirror failover test, 3) corrupt-bytes test where GET returns wrong bytes but HEAD passes, verify detection.
zane: also add a chaos test that deletes a random shard mid-warmup and asserts either warmup aborts (strict) or partial state + fallback routing (tolerant).
devon: I'll prototype preflight HEAD+read-first-N and the retry logic. plan to land as a feature-flag behind loader.v1.toggle.fallback-safety.
deploy-bot: deploy: loader-service v1.3.2 -> canary started (nodes: canary-04..canary-07). commit: add preflight skeleton + retries.
erin: thanks. followups: maria-r to PR manifest delta; devon to prototype preflight; sam_k to add tests; zane to update routing fallbacks. we'll sync in async; please drop short notes in the RFC follow-up doc. :thumbsup:
